title: Porsche 911 Engines by Year (1965–2026)
description: Every factory engine in the US Porsche 911 by year, 1965–2026: the air-cooled sixes and 930 Turbo, the water-cooled M96, Mezger and 9A engines, and the T-Hybrid.
intro: Porsche brought the 911 to the US for 1965, and every one has had a flat-six engine. US cars were often rated below European ones because of emissions equipment. Where Porsche quoted a US car only in metric (DIN) horsepower, the rating is shown in PS. Hybrid ratings are for engine and motor combined.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.

generations.name: Original 911
intro: The 2.0, 2.2 and 2.4 air-cooled sixes in the 911, 911T, E, S and L.

generations.name: G-series
intro: The 2.7, the 3.0 SC and the 3.2 Carrera, plus the 3.0 and 3.3 930 Turbo (not sold in the US 1980–1985).
The 3.6 M64, the 3.3 Turbo and the 1994 3.6 Turbo.
The last air-cooled 911s: the 3.6, the Varioram 3.6 and the twin-turbo 3.6.
The first water-cooled 911s: the 3.4 and 3.6 M96, and the Mezger engines of the Turbo, GT2 and GT3.
The 3.6 and 3.8 M97, direct-injection 9A1 engines from 2009, and the Mezger Turbo, GT2 and GT3.
The 3.4 and 3.8 9A1, the 3.0 twin-turbo 9A2 from 2017, and the 4.0 GT engines.
The 3.0 twin-turbo 9A2 Evo, the 3.7 Turbo, the 4.0 GT3, and the 3.6 T-Hybrid from 2025.

method: Every engine and year listed here was confirmed by at least three independent sources: the NHRA Stock Car Classification Guides, factory material such as GM Heritage Center information kits and sales brochures, EPA records and established references. Several Wikipedia articles count as one source. Where sources give different ratings, the factory figure is shown and the difference is noted. Factory race-only packages need two sources.
